claim: The low-case normalized total is 37,584 metric tonnes per year.

notes: Company-program concentration, not facility output concentration.

claim: MP targets 3,000 tpa at Independence and 7,000 tpa at 10X, with 10X commissioning expected in 2028.
MP remained in qualification and start-up ahead of commercial production in Q2 2026.
USAR commissioned Phase 1a and targets 600 tpa by Q4 2026, while its combined U.S. program targets 10,000 tpa.
eVAC publicly reported commercial shipments and approximately 2,000 tpa nameplate capacity.
Noveon publicly reported commercial deliveries and capacity beyond a 2,000-ton baseline, but did not define the unit or expanded capacity.
Vulcan’s Benson project targets 10,000 metric tonnes per year.
JS Link’s Georgia project targets 3,000 tons per year and late-2027 operations, with the ton unit unspecified.
HyProMag’s full design contains 673 tpa finished magnets and 375 tpa sintered blocks; 478 tpa of powder/swarf co-products is excluded.
The Commerce/DOE 37,000-tonne 2030 forecast is total demand, including magnets embedded in imported goods.
Commerce reported about 7,500 tonnes of direct sintered NdFeB magnet imports in 2021 and cited a DLA estimate that embedded imports supplied 60% of essential civilian demand.
notes: Historical baseline, not a 2026 direct-demand estimate.

claim: Commerce says total, direct and embedded demand estimates should be approached with caution because the supply chain is opaque.
Commerce reports 54-81% recovery from alloy to finished magnet and notes that machining swarf is often recycled.
Full utilization of the audited capacity implies roughly 46,400-70,459 tonnes per year of gross alloy process flow at 81-54% recovery.
At 30% rare-earth content, the gross process-flow range contains roughly 13,920-21,138 tonnes of rare earths.
China accounted for 94% of sintered permanent-magnet production in 2024, while magnet manufacturing and metallisation remain the main diversification bottlenecks.
Capacity tonnes are not fungible across blocks, finished shapes, grades, coatings and qualification regimes.
notes: Mechanically supported by product-form disclosures and qualification status.

claim: The project stack does not by itself prove independence from Chinese supply.
